A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STPGC research, with matching authors, algorithms, and theoretical foundations. All pages, including appendices, tables, figures, and proofs, support comparison despite the revised title and expanded evaluation.

before.justification: v1 reports original node-classification, runtime, memory, topology-preservation, sensitivity, and scalability results, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds link prediction, graph classification, heterophilic-graph evaluation, and edge-perturbation experiments in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The three collapse/coning algorithms, exact and approximate phases, relaxed dominance condition, and feature/label aggregation remain unchanged. DropEdge and the implementation optimizations were already documented in v1's Appendix C; their appearance in v2's main text does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Appendices D.3–D.6 add link prediction on Cora, Citeseer, and DBLP; graph classification on MUTAG and Peptides-func; heterophilic node classification on Texas, Wisconsin, and Cornell; and perturbed-edge scenarios on Cora. This substantially extends the previous node-classification and scalability coverage.

E2.justification: UGC and MPG are added to the retained node-classification comparison on Cora, Citeseer, and DBLP at c=0.5, 0.3, and 0.1 in v2 Table 1, corresponding to v1 Table 2. This is a limited expansion of the existing comparator suite; they are not added to the runtime table or the c=0.2 comparison.

E3.justification: Scalability sampling changes from random node/edge sampling to reported BFS sampling over 10%–100% of nodes. Figure 7 changes its degree thresholds from 30/50/70/100 to 5/10/15/20. New experiments introduce AUC/AP evaluation, GIN and GPRGNN settings, and 10%/20% edge perturbations. Table 3 also revises DBLP's nodes/edges/features from 3,877/16,624/1,700 to 17,716/52,867/1,639, without establishing whether this corrects documentation or reflects rerun experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix D.6 adds a focused robustness test: randomly adding or deleting 10% and 20% of Cora's edges before coarsening, evaluated with GCN at three coarsening ratios. The existing Betti-number and degree-threshold analyses remain; no new component ablation is introduced.

E5.justification: Retained classification tables continue using the same ± reporting convention. Neither version specifies run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added appendix tables provide point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds UGC/MPG results and Tables 5–8, and revises existing scores. Under matching reported settings, ArXiv GCN accuracy at c=0.5 changes from 70.4±0.3 to 69.6±0.3, while Cora APPNP at c=0.2 changes from 83.9±0.3 to 84.9±0.3. Scalability curves also change under revised sampling and threshold settings, so those differences are not same-setting speed improvements.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.4 corrects its statement from reducing a node to reducing an edge via GEdgeCollapse. This aligns it with the existing edge-deletion proof in Appendix A.4. The remaining definitions, proofs, and complexity analyses are substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The main topology-preservation, GNN-acceleration, and claimed 37x speedup contributions remain. The conclusion adds an explicit generality claim that one coarsened graph can serve as preprocessing for any downstream GNN pipeline without modifying its architecture.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly confines shortest-path guarantees to ExactCoarsening and acknowledges limitations of heuristic feature averaging and majority-vote labels. Appendix D.1 narrows universal superiority to competitive performance. The scalability explanation changes from accelerated edge growth to BFS sampling of dense cores followed by inexpensive peripheral nodes.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds a code-repository address and explicitly describes training/validation on coarsened graphs followed by inference on the original graph. The PyTorch Geometric implementation, degree thresholds, and DropEdge settings were already disclosed in v1's Appendix C and are repeated in v2's main text.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for UGC, MPG, GPRGNN, GIN, MUTAG, and the long-range graph benchmark to support expanded comparisons and evaluations. Section 5's research-positioning narrative remains essentially unchanged; corrected publication years for existing references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'Scalable Topology-Preserving Graph Coarsening: Concepts and Algorithms.' v2 adds affiliation/conference information and acknowledgments, makes local language corrections, expands selected discussions, and organizes Appendix D into numbered subsections with a new Appendix E. Most existing exposition and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds four experimental tables and the topology illustration in Figure 11, expands the main accuracy table, and redraws scalability Figures 6–7. It also consolidates legends, clarifies parameter-axis labels, and relocates several displays, including reversing the numbering of the accuracy and runtime tables. These materially expand and revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The added comparators and cross-task/robustness evaluations provide more informative evidence about applicability, while code-access information and explicit limitations improve transparency. The gains are limited by sparse protocols and absent uncertainty reporting for the new experiments, plus unexplained revisions to existing results. Some discussion is not reconciled with the tables: Section 4 still singles out ArXiv exceptions at c=0.1 and 0.2, although v2 Table 1 also places GCN below GEC at c=0.5 and 0.3.
